market_summary: Markets are digesting a violent post-midterm selloff (Nasdaq -5.5%, S&P -4.4% Thu) driven by fears of tighter AI regulation and slowing data-center capex, followed by a partial stabilization Friday as semis bounced ~4.2%. Mega-cap AI names remain the epicenter: Nvidia is dealing with a fresh, serious governance shock (CEO Jensen Huang affair/security investigation disclosed Nov 8), while Alphabet faces scrutiny over its $75.7bn of data-center credit backstops even as it unveils new TPU chips to compete with Nvidia. In Singapore, Q3 bank earnings were mixed — OCBC beat while DBS and UOB missed amid NIM pressure — and all three plus the STI ETF are down sharply over 1-3 months with elevated volume, suggesting a broader de-rating of the banking sector rather than single-name issues. Overall risk appetite is fragile and headline-driven, favoring tactical, catalyst-based positioning over broad beta bets.

picks.thesis: A CEO-level governance and national-security scandal (alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, board investigation launched) adds a serious idiosyncratic overhang on top of an already weak technical picture (-19% 1m, trading 15% below its 50-day average). Headline risk is likely to stay elevated into the Nov 17 earnings date, and further disclosures from the investigation could pressure the stock even as today's bounce reflects broader semis relief rather than resolution of the Nvidia-specific issue.
picks.news: Nvidia board launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy; Huang admitted the affair in a letter to employees raising security concerns (both Nov 8, 2026).
picks.risks: If the investigation clears Huang quickly or is deemed immaterial to operations, the stock could resume tracking broader semiconductor sentiment, which rebounded 4.2% on Nov 8 on dip-buying; strong Nov 17 earnings could also override the scandal narrative.

picks.thesis: Alphabet is down ~18-20% over the past month and quarter on AI capex concerns, and fresh reporting today shows lenders are starting to question the durability of Alphabet's $75.7bn in data-center credit backstops — a new, negative financing-related catalyst that could keep pressure on the stock even as the new TPU 8t/8i chips are a modestly positive offsetting headline. The stock remains ~14.5% below its 50-day average with no sign of basing yet.
picks.news: Report on lender scrutiny of Alphabet's $75.7bn data-center credit backstops (Nov 9, 2026); $17bn Wyoming data center investment announced amid AI capex concerns (Nov 5, 2026); Citizens downgraded GOOGL from Outperform to Market Perform on Oct 29.
picks.risks: GOOGL's new TPU chips directly challenging Nvidia could be read bullishly if they win meaningful cloud/AI workload share, and the stock is already down heavily, raising the odds of a sharp short-covering bounce; strong analyst support (53 buy ratings) also argues for caution on the short thesis.

picks.thesis: OCBC beat Q3 estimates while DBS and UOB both missed, yet all three SGX banks sold off together this week amid a broader de-rating of the sector on NIM pressure concerns — OCBC's relative earnings strength versus its peers suggests it is the most likely to recover first if sentiment stabilizes, and it still carries ~12% implied upside to consensus target.
picks.news: OCBC beat Q3 estimates while DBS and UOB missed (Nov 6, 2026); Singapore bank earnings weighed on the STI amid NIM pressure concerns (Nov 6, 2026).
picks.risks: If NIM compression proves sector-wide and structural (rate environment), OCBC's earnings beat may not be enough to decouple it from a broader de-rating; continued index-wide selling (STI ETF rel. volume 2.24x normal) could keep dragging all three banks down together.

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 estimates and carries the weakest analyst skew of the three Singapore banks (only 4 buys vs 10 holds/2 sells), yet it has fallen the most (-8.4% 1m, -12.5% 3m, -11.2% vs 50-day average) and remains below its 200-day average, unlike DBS and OCBC which are still above theirs — suggesting UOB is the weakest link in a sector facing NIM pressure.
picks.news: UOB missed Q3 earnings estimates amid NIM pressure that weighed on the broader STI banking complex (Nov 6, 2026).
picks.risks: UOB's high relative volume (1.98x) and steep drawdown already price in much of the bad news; a sector-wide relief rally (e.g., rate-cut expectations improving NIM outlook) would likely lift UOB along with peers and squeeze shorts.

picks.thesis: Keppel shows a clear technical breakdown — down 4.9% today alone, -9.9% over 1 month, -28.2% from its 52-week high, with unusually heavy relative volume (2.57x) suggesting active distribution. No specific fresh news was found to explain the move, which is itself a caution flag that something company- or sector-specific may be driving the sell-off that hasn't yet hit mainstream coverage.
picks.news: No dated news item on Keppel was available in this research cycle; the move is being inferred purely from price/volume behavior.
picks.risks: This is a technical-only view with no confirmed news catalyst; analysts remain very bullish (12 buy/2 hold/1 sell, 34.5% implied upside), and this could simply be a temporary, market-wide de-risking move that reverses quickly, especially if it turns out to be correlated with the broader Thursday/Friday volatility rather than Keppel-specific news.
